name: Naloxone
status: DRAFT – pharmacology (†) is not yet checked against the package insert; doses are extracted automatically from the guideline text
dagger_note: † = general pharmacology; not in the SA guideline and not yet checked against the package insert
item_format: t=text, s=source:printed page, d=dagger, b=bold, h=heading

moa.t: Competitive antagonist at μ, κ and δ opioid receptors, short half-life (shorter than most opioids)

dosing_note: Doses are extracted automatically from the guideline text. Each heading is the nearest section title in the guideline and can be off by one section – confirm on the cited page. The pathway dose stays authoritative for its indication.

items.t: Naloxone, IV, 0.4 mg immediately, in patients with significant respiratory depression. · Effectiveness is limited by a half-life (± 1 hour) that is shorter than
Naloxone, IV, 0.1 mg/kg. Naloxone is not routinely indicated for neonatal resuscitation.
Naloxone, IV/IM, 0.1 mg/kg. » Maternal » Corrects apnoea · May need repeating after 2 hours. administration of and/or opiates with hypoventilation.
Naloxone, IV, 0.1 mg/kg: · If no response after 5 minutes, repeat dose and titrate according to response.

adjustments.t: Use when indicated; may precipitate withdrawal in an opioid-dependent mother or neonate

cautions.t: Re-sedation is likely – observe and repeat or infuse
Titrate small doses in dependent patients to restore breathing, not full wakefulness

adverse_effects.t: Acute withdrawal in dependent patients (agitation, vomiting), hypertension, pulmonary oedema (rare)

monitoring.t: Respiratory rate, saturation, level of consciousness for hours after the last dose
